artifacts.title: Senters v. Savannah River Presbytery

Presbyteries often assign credential-related examinations, including transfer exams, to established committees such as CCC, and often Presbyteries follow recommendations of those committees, but it is the Presbytery itself that is charged with conducting and a

artifacts.synopsis: TE David Senters complained that Savannah River Presbytery erred by judging TE Stamberg's stated difference with WCF 21.3 regarding the gift of tongues as 'not a difference' during a transfer examination. The SJC denied the procedural part of the complaint but sustained the confessional part, finding it was error to conclude Stamberg's view on continuing tongues was not a difference with WCF 1.1 and 1.6, and remanded to Presbytery for further action.

artifacts.title: Frazier v. Nashville Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: TE Frazier complained that Nashville Presbytery erred in finding insufficient evidence to raise a strong presumption of guilt against TE Scott Sauls regarding his teaching on same-sex attraction; the SJC denied the complaint 20-0-1, concluding NP fulfilled its BCO 31-2 investigatory duties, accompanied by several concurring opinions raising procedural and exegetical concerns.

A candidate for licensure is required to demonstrate basic knowledge of the Book of Church Order. (BCO 19-2, b-3). He is not, however, required to make any personal affirmations regarding his approval of it. Nevertheless, the licensure examination in this matt

artifacts.synopsis: The Session of Crossroads Community Church challenged Philadelphia Presbytery's licensing and ordination of a candidate who stated a difference concerning women and the office of deacon but agreed to follow the BCO. The SJC denied the complaint and affirmed presbytery's judgment, holding that the candidate's stated willingness to comply with the BCO and affirm the ordination vow supported the decision; a dissent argued the complaint should have been sustained.

artifacts.title: Extraordinary clause exemptions from licensure examinations

matches.evidence: In extraordinary cases a presbytery may exempt a candidate from any of the prescribed parts of the licensure examination under BCO 19-2, though the clause must not be used as a subterfuge to avoid historic training requirements.

artifacts.title: Written sermon requirement for licensure under BCO 19-2

matches.evidence: Both a written and oral sermon are required for licensure; the written sermon must be available to the full presbytery, while the oral sermon may be presented before the presbytery or its committee.

artifacts.title: Administrative Committee acting as an unlimited commission under Standing Rule 16

matches.evidence: The CCB advised that Standing Rule 16 effectively created an unlimited commission contrary to BCO 15-1, which restricts commissions to specifically defined matters.
